name: Dark Pink
lede: Dark Pink is a descriptive name for a deep, slightly bluish pink; the swatch comes from a 2010 color survey, and the phrase turns up in the books for a flower and for a ruined painting.

sections.title: A modifier, not a history
sections.body: The swatch is from the xkcd color survey of 2010, and the nearest ISCC-NBS name is "strong purplish red", 5.1 units away [1]. The words *dark pink* are older than the swatch, and two books use them for real things. For the plain rose-pink side of the family, see [[rose]].

sections.title: A flower on an indigo plant
sections.body: Balfour-Paul describes the dyer's knotweed, *Polygonum tinctorium*, an indigo plant of East Asia (compare [[indigo]]), whose small flowers range from white to dark pink [2]. Some growers believe the pink-flowered plants give more dye [2].

sections.title: Rothko's Harvard murals
sections.body: Ball reports that the dominant colors of Mark Rothko's Harvard murals, given to the university in 1962, were dark pink and [[crimson]] [3]. He made the reds from mixtures including two modern colorants, Naphthol Red, which lasted, and Lithol Red, which is very fugitive in light [3]. Within five years the murals were deteriorating, and by 1979 they were removed from view; Ball says they have turned light blue [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Only 2 of 23,781 archive paintings contain it, rarer than 86 per cent of named colors, and the one dated example is from 1924, by Patrick Henry Bruce [4]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, so the count says little about how painters have used [[pink]] [4].
